course_name_original: Geometrische und numerische Methoden für Informatiker
course_name_en: Geometric and Numerical Methods for Computer Scientists
prerequisites: In-depth knowledge of analysis and linear algebra, as acquired in introductory mathematics modules (e.g., Mathematics 1 to 3 for MI/TI).

learning_outcomes.text: Students master fundamental algorithms of geometry and numerical methods, they know and understand applications of these mathematical methods in computer graphics, animation, simulation, signal and image processing.
Students possess in-depth knowledge of geometric and numerical methods.

Students evaluate geometric and numerical methods regarding the conditions and consequences of their use and apply these methods to solve problems in a subject-specific manner. They critically interpret the results from the perspective of their specific application.
Students evaluate and use procedures and methods of numerical analysis and geometry in the context of computer graphics, animation, simulation and numerical data analysis.
Students can present the results of their term paper, competently explain their solution approaches and procedures, and present them orally and in writing.

syllabus_topics: Calculation and representation of curves and surfaces with applications in computer graphics and animation
Numerical solution methods for linear and nonlinear equations and systems
Elementary numerical methods for differential equations
Integral transformations and their applications in computer science

assessment_methods.method: Term paper (written elaboration and oral explanation)

assessment_rules: The graded assessment consists of a term paper, which includes a written elaboration (approx. 10-15 pages) and an oral explanation (approx. 15-20 minutes). An ungraded assessment requires regular attendance, meaning at least 80% presence in the course.
